title: Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT: Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo Solvers for Single- and Multi-Orbital Hubbard Model
abstract: We present two related customized software packages, Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT, designed to solve the Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) equations for strongly correlated electron systems. Hubb_DMFT is adjusted for the single-band Hubbard model, providing a fast way to calculate the local self-energy, as well as the two-particle fermion and triangular fermion-boson charge and spin vertices, while Wan2mb_DMFT extends this capability to realistic multi-orbital systems, directly interfacing Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians with many-body solvers. Both codes are based on iQIST v.0.7 impurity solver and utilize a modified and internally integrated Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo (CT-QMC) core with the hybridization expansion (CT-HYB) framework and improved self-energy and vertex estimators for density-density interaction, ensuring numerically exact solutions for quantum impurity problems.
summary: This paper details two advanced software packages, Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT, designed to solve the DMFT equations for strongly correlated electron systems. They employ a Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo solver within the CT-HYB framework to calculate key observables like the self-energy and interaction vertices. The work is significant for providing robust tools to study correlated materials ranging from simple Hubbard models to complex multi-orbital systems like TMDs.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of solving the Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DMFT) equations for strongly correlated electron systems.
main_result: It introduces two specialized software packages, Hubb_DMFT and Wan2mb_DMFT, capable of calculating local self-energies and two-particle vertices for both single-band and multi-orbital Hubbard models.
method: The core method is based on a self-consistent DMFT loop utilizing a modified Continuous-Time Quantum Monte Carlo (CT-QMC) solver within the Hybridization Expansion (CT-HYB) framework.
model_or_system: The models studied are the single-band and multi-orbital Hubbard models. The multi-orbital extension specifically interfaces with Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians derived from DFT calculations.
key_observables: Local self-energy ($\Sigma$), local Green's function ($G_{	ext{local}}$), and two-particle fermion/triangular fermion-boson charge and spin vertices.
important_parameters: Coulomb interaction ($U, V_q$), hopping parameters ($t_{ij}$), and orbital parameters ($U, J_H$). Benchmark studies use parameters like $U = 5.6t$ for cuprate models.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the CT-HYB algorithm for achieving numerically exact solutions for the quantum impurity problem. Multi-orbital calculations require careful handling of double-counting corrections.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows calculated $\Sigma$ and triangular vertices for the 2D Hubbard model. Figure 3 shows similar results for a $	ext{CrTe}_2$ monolayer, demonstrating orbital-dependent correlation effects.
paper_structure: The paper presents the two codes, Hubb_DMFT (single-band) and Wan2mb_DMFT (multi-orbital), detailing their implementation using the CT-QMC/CT-HYB framework. It outlines the self-consistent loop structure and provides benchmarks on physical systems like the 2D Hubbard model and TMDs.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state correlation, the use of advanced quantum Monte Carlo techniques and the development of highly specialized, numerically exact solvers for many-body Hamiltonians are relevant to understanding complex quantum dynamics in open quantum systems.
